questions.reviewer_concern: Why did the pipeline register MissForest/MICE when executor_stage5b.py executed univariate SimpleImputer(strategy='median')?
questions.honest_answer: The synthesis taxonomy associated the missing-value slot with MICE/MissForest literature citations, but the operational tabular executor implemented train-fitted univariate median/mode imputation. The paper transparently reports median/mode imputation as the operational path.
questions.evidence: Section 3.10 and Abstract explicitly state the tabular benchmark evaluated median/mode imputation.

questions.reviewer_concern: Why are cross-attention and average ensembling in the pipeline specification if they were not executed in the HANCOCK benchmark?
questions.honest_answer: Cross-attention and ensembling belong to the general multimodal synthesis taxonomy. Because the benchmark evaluated unimodal clinical tables, these modules remained dormant. The empirical results are not claimed as validating them.
questions.evidence: Section 3.10, Figure 1 caption, and Figure 7 caption formally classify them as EVIDENCE_BACKED_BUT_DORMANT.

questions.reviewer_concern: Is progress_1 (binary disease progression) an outcome proxy for recurrence?
questions.honest_answer: In retrospective clinical records, progression can coincide with recurrence timing. The paper explicitly scopes the task as Post-Adjuvant Recurrence Risk Prediction and documents progress_1 as a prospective deployment caveat requiring exclusion.
questions.evidence: Section 4.2 explicitly identifies progress_1 and distinguishes retrospective benchmark validity from prospective deployment validity.

questions.reviewer_concern: At what exact clinical timepoint does this model make predictions?
questions.honest_answer: The model operates at the Post-Adjuvant Therapy Completion epoch (predicting subsequent recurrence given surgical and adjuvant therapy).
questions.evidence: Section 4.1 formally defines the task as Post-Adjuvant Recurrence Risk Prediction.

questions.reviewer_concern: The Simple MLP baseline used max_iter=10. Is this an intentionally weak strawman?
questions.honest_answer: Yes, a 10-iteration MLP is severely underconverged. The paper explicitly characterizes Simple MLP as a shallow, minimal reference baseline and retracts any claim of superiority over deep learning.
questions.evidence: Section 4.4 and Section 5.1 state that Simple MLP is a minimal reference baseline and does not establish superiority over optimized neural architectures.

questions.reviewer_concern: Is a +0.0047 ROC-AUC gain over Default XGBoost practically meaningful?
questions.honest_answer: The margin is modest (+0.48% relative). The primary value of the work is the provenance-aware synthesis and governance methodology, not a large performance leap.
questions.evidence: Abstract, Section 5.1, and Section 6 explicitly describe the margin as modest.

questions.reviewer_concern: The candidate pipeline lost to Default XGBoost on Seed 100 (0.9609 vs 0.9643). Does this undermine the claim of baseline superiority?
questions.honest_answer: The candidate won 2 out of 3 seeds (66.7% win rate) but does not dominate all folds. The paper transparently reports the Seed 100 loss and disavows universal superiority.
questions.evidence: Table 2, Section 5.2, and Figure 3 explicitly present the Seed 100 loss.

questions.reviewer_concern: Why did Ablation B (Without SMOTE: 0.9773) and Ablation D (Ordinal: 0.9784) outperform the Full Candidate (0.9751)?
questions.honest_answer: Evidence-backed validity represents physiological/clinical justification from literature, which does not guarantee empirical optimality on a single retrospective sample. SMOTE can introduce minor boundary noise in low-dimensional clinical tables.
questions.evidence: Section 5.3 and Section 6.2 thoroughly discuss why evidence validity != empirical dataset optimality.

questions.reviewer_concern: Is n=3 random seeds sufficient for statistical significance?
questions.honest_answer: No. The sample size is underpowered for inferential hypothesis testing. The paper makes strictly descriptive claims and suppresses p-values.
questions.evidence: Section 5.2 and Section 8 explicitly document n=3 as a statistical limitation.

questions.reviewer_concern: Can these findings generalize to external medical centers?
questions.honest_answer: Generalizability has not been established. Evaluation is restricted to the single-center retrospective HANCOCK cohort.
questions.evidence: Section 8 and Section 9 list multi-center external validation as essential future work.

questions.reviewer_concern: Is this pipeline ready for clinical deployment in oncology clinics?
questions.honest_answer: No. The framework is a research methodology. Prospective clinical trials and decision-curve analyses are required before any clinical deployment.
questions.evidence: Section 8 explicitly states the model is NOT clinically deployable.

questions.reviewer_concern: How does this differ from standard AutoML tools like TPOT or Auto-sklearn?
questions.honest_answer: AutoML conducts unconstrained empirical optimization over arbitrary search spaces without provenance. Evidence-conditioned synthesis constrains composition strictly to literature-grounded mechanisms and explicit configuration gates.
questions.evidence: Section 2.2 and Section 7.1 provide a detailed 3-level novelty breakdown comparing evidence synthesis to AutoML.

questions.reviewer_concern: Can a 4-paper literature corpus demonstrate generalizable literature synthesis?
questions.honest_answer: The 4-paper corpus serves as an end-to-end proof-of-concept for the synthesis methodology. Future work must scale to automated broader retrieval.
questions.evidence: Section 8 and Section 9 acknowledge corpus size limitations.

questions.reviewer_concern: Why were one-hot encoding and binary logistic loss configured manually rather than extracted from literature?
questions.honest_answer: When literature evidence is absent, the framework halts automated inference and enforces a human configuration gate, preventing silent library defaults.
questions.evidence: Section 3.9 rigorously segregates EVIDENCE_BACKED from EXPLICITLY_CONFIGURED primitives.

questions.reviewer_concern: If omitting SMOTE improved ROC-AUC (0.9773), why was SMOTE selected in the candidate pipeline?
questions.honest_answer: SMOTE was selected a priori because literature evidence (PMID: 41006422) reported its necessity for imbalanced recurrence classification. Retaining it preserves the audit integrity of evidence-conditioned selection without post-hoc cherry-picking.
questions.evidence: Section 5.3 and Section 6.2 discuss SMOTE selection and ablation behavior.

questions.reviewer_concern: Were imputers or encoders fitted on test data?
questions.honest_answer: No. All imputers, encoders, and resamplers were fitted strictly on the training partition within each seed fold.
questions.evidence: Section 4.3 and backend test suites verify train-only fitting.

questions.reviewer_concern: Was there any patient overlap between training, validation, and test splits?
questions.honest_answer: Zero patient overlap. Patient IDs were stratified and cryptographically hashed with strict set intersection = 0.
questions.evidence: Section 4.1 and Stage 5B executor verification confirm zero overlap.

questions.reviewer_concern: Does a Brier score of 0.0175 prove clinical calibration?
questions.honest_answer: It demonstrates low statistical probability error on internal test partitions, but does not substitute for prospective clinical calibration assessment.
questions.evidence: Section 5.4 and Section 6.3 frame Brier scores conservatively.

questions.reviewer_concern: Can another researcher independently reproduce these exact results?
questions.honest_answer: Yes. Execution is fully deterministic across fixed seeds [42, 100, 2026] and governed by immutable SHA-256 contract hashes.
questions.evidence: Section 3.12 and reproducibility manifests provide complete verification hashes.

questions.reviewer_concern: Why did Random Forest (0.9698) and Default XGBoost (0.9704) perform so close to Candidate (0.9751)?
questions.honest_answer: Tree-based algorithms naturally capture non-linear interactions among structured clinical tabular features, creating a high baseline performance ceiling.
questions.evidence: Section 5.1 and Section 6.1 analyze tree baseline dynamics.

questions.reviewer_concern: Does the system assess the risk of bias in extracted literature papers?
questions.honest_answer: Not currently. Integrating automated study appraisal (e.g., PROBAST / Cochrane criteria) is planned as future work.
questions.evidence: Section 9.2 lists automated risk-of-bias scoring as a future priority.

questions.reviewer_concern: What missingness rate was present in the HANCOCK tabular data?
questions.honest_answer: Structured clinical tabular covariates had moderate missingness (e.g., smoking status, treatment modality), which was handled via train-fitted median/mode imputation.
questions.evidence: Section 4.3 documents train-only tabular imputation.

questions.reviewer_concern: What were the compute requirements for pipeline synthesis and execution?
questions.honest_answer: Execution took 6.87 seconds with peak RAM of 6.83 MB on CPU, well within the 4 GB / 15-minute budget.
questions.evidence: Section 3.12 and contract verification document compute compliance.

questions.reviewer_concern: Does this paper follow established clinical ML reporting guidelines?
questions.honest_answer: Yes, the methodology is aligned with TRIPOD+AI and PROBAST reporting principles for leakage prevention and split transparency.
questions.evidence: Section 2.3 contextualizes the framework within reporting standards.

questions.reviewer_concern: What is the primary takeaway if the candidate model is just an XGBoost classifier?
questions.honest_answer: The primary takeaway is the evidence-conditioned synthesis methodology and governance framework that systematically builds valid, leakage-firewalled ML pipelines from biomedical literature with end-to-end traceability.
questions.evidence: Abstract, Section 1, Section 7, and Section 9 emphasize the methodological framework.
